learn.hook: One sheet of paper, a few folds and a puddle. What do you get? A boat!
points: The lesson 'Paper Boats' is a poem about making paper boats and floating them in rainwater.
Some words copy sounds, like 'pitter-patter' for falling rain.
Rhyming words at the line ends give a poem its music: rain – lane, wide – side.
Read the poem with a rhythm, as if raindrops are tapping.

example.q:
Read our poem:
Pitter-patter goes the rain,
Puddles fill our little lane.
I fold my paper, one, two, three,
A tiny boat for you and me.
It bobs along the puddle wide,
With a leaf for a friend by its side.
What is floating next to the boat?
steps: Find the last line: 'With a leaf for a friend by its side.'
'by its side' means next to it.
So a leaf is floating next to the boat.

learn.reallife: When it rains, you can make a paper boat with an elder and float it in a small puddle in your courtyard.

games.title: True or false? (about our poem)
items: In the poem, puddles fill the lane.
The second line says 'Puddles fill our little lane.'
The child in the poem makes a paper plane.
The child makes a tiny paper boat.
The poem says 'Pitter-patter goes the rain.'
In the poem, the boat sails on a big river.

games.title: Match the word to its meaning
pairs: a small pool of water on the ground
to move gently up and down

quiz.q: Read: 'Pitter-patter goes the rain.' What is 'pitter-patter'?
quiz.explain: 'Pitter-patter' copies the sound of raindrops falling.
steps: 'Pitter-patter goes the rain' copies the sound of raindrops.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that some words copy sounds

quiz.q: Read: 'Puddles fill our little lane.' What fills the lane?
quiz.explain: The line says puddles fill the lane.
steps: Find the line: 'Puddles fill our little lane.'
quiz.mistake: Did not read the line carefully

quiz.q: Read: 'I fold my paper, one, two, three, / A tiny boat for you and me.' What does the child make?
quiz.explain: The child folds paper to make a tiny boat.
steps: Find the lines: 'I fold my paper… A tiny boat for you and me.'
quiz.mistake: Mixes up boats with other paper toys

quiz.q: Read: 'It bobs along the puddle wide.' What does 'bobs' mean here?
quiz.explain: A boat bobs when it moves up and down on the water.
steps: The boat floats on the puddle.
'bobs' means it moves gently up and down.
It does not sink. Answer: moves gently up and down
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'bob'

quiz.q: Read: 'With a leaf for a friend by its side.' What floats by the boat's side?
quiz.explain: The line says a leaf is its friend by its side.
steps: Find the line: 'With a leaf for a friend by its side.'
quiz.mistake: Guessed instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'rain'?
quiz.explain: 'rain' and 'lane' both end with the '-ain' / '-ane' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that only begins the same way

quiz.q: Which pair of words from the boat poem rhymes?
quiz.explain: 'three' and 'me' end with the same '-ee' sound.
steps: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks words that go together in meaning but do not rhyme

quiz.q: A poem has rain, puddles and a paper boat. Which season is it most likely about?
quiz.explain: Rain and puddles tell us it is the rainy season.
steps: The poem has rain and puddles.
Rain and puddles come in the rainy season.
quiz.mistake: Did not use the clues rain and puddles

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What happens in the paper boat poem? Which words rhyme?'
teach.praise: Pitter-patter! I want to float a paper boat too!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what the child makes in the poem and two words that rhyme?

revise.summary: 'Paper Boats' is a poem about making paper boats and floating them in rainwater. It uses sound words like 'pitter-patter' and rhyming words like rain – lane.
focus: Finding what each line tells us
Rhyming pairs: rain – lane, three – me, wide – side
remember: Rhymes: rain – lane, three – me, wide – side
traps: Rhyming words end the same; 'rain' and 'rainy' do not rhyme
The leaf floats by the boat; it is not a duck or fish

learn.hook: Drip, drop, splash! What is your favourite thing to do on a rainy day?
points: Rain words: drizzle (light rain), downpour (very heavy rain), puddle, umbrella, raincoat.
The monsoon is the rainy season in India.
Lightning is the bright flash in the sky. Thunder is the loud sound that comes with it.
When there is thunder and lightning, go indoors. Never stand under a tree.
When the sun shines after rain, we may see a rainbow.

example.q: It is drizzling and Sonu wants to float his paper boat. Lightning flashes in the sky. What should he do?
steps: Drizzle is light rain, so a small puddle is fun to play in.
When there is lightning, it is safest to go indoors.
example.answer: Sonu should go indoors and play later, when the storm is over.

learn.reallife: In the monsoon you wear a raincoat, carry an umbrella and jump over puddles on the way to school.

games.title: Safe or not safe?
items: floating a boat in a small puddle with an elder
standing under a tree when there is lightning
touching an electric pole in the rain
drying your feet when you come home

quiz.q: What is light rain called?
quiz.explain: A drizzle is light rain with tiny drops.
steps: Drizzle = light rain; downpour = very heavy rain.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up light rain with heavy rain

quiz.q: What do we carry to stay dry in the rain?
quiz.explain: An umbrella keeps the rain off us.
steps: An umbrella keeps the rain off us.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which things keep us dry

quiz.q: What is the loud, rumbling sound in the sky during a storm?
quiz.explain: Thunder is the sound. Lightning is the flash we see.
steps: Lightning is the flash; thunder is the loud sound.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up thunder and lightning

quiz.q: What is the bright flash of light in the sky during a storm?
quiz.explain: Lightning is the flash. Thunder is the sound.
steps: Thunder is the sound; lightning is the bright flash.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up lightning and thunder

quiz.q: There is thunder and lightning. Where is the safest place to be?
quiz.explain: Indoors is safest during lightning. Trees, fields and roofs are not safe.
steps: Rule: with thunder and lightning, go indoors.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a tree is a safe shelter in a storm

quiz.q: What does the word 'monsoon' mean?
quiz.explain: The monsoon is the rainy season in India.
steps: The monsoon is the rainy season in India.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word 'monsoon'

quiz.q: What might you see in the sky when the sun shines after rain?
quiz.explain: Sunlight shining through raindrops can make a rainbow.
steps: When the sun shines after rain, we may see a rainbow.
quiz.mistake: Does not know when rainbows appear

quiz.q: What is a small pool of rainwater on the ground called?
quiz.explain: A puddle is a small pool of water left by rain.
steps: Rain leaves small pools of water on the ground.
Such a pool is a puddle.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a puddle with bigger bodies of water

teach.ask: Gappu's feathers are wet! He asks: 'What are some rain words? How do I stay safe in a storm?'
teach.praise: I will fly indoors when it thunders! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me some rain words and what to do when there is lightning?

revise.summary: Rain words include drizzle, downpour, puddle, umbrella and raincoat. The monsoon is India's rainy season; during thunder and lightning we must go indoors.
remember: Drizzle = light rain; downpour = very heavy rain
traps: Never stand under a tree in thunder and lightning
Don't mix up thunder and lightning

learn.hook: One boat, two boats, three boats... What changes when there is more than one?
points: Singular means one: a boat. Plural means more than one: boats.
Most words just add -s: boat – boats, puddle – puddles.
Words ending in s, sh, ch or x add -es: bus – buses, dish – dishes, box – boxes.
Some words ending in y change y to ies: baby – babies.
Some words change in a special way: child – children, leaf – leaves, foot – feet.

steps: Look at the ending of 'bench': it ends in 'ch'.

learn.reallife: At the market Mummy asks for 'six bananas' or 'two boxes of sweets'. You use plurals all the time!

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'boat'?
quiz.explain: Most words just add -s: boat – boats.
quiz.mistake: Adds -es when only -s is needed

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'box'?
quiz.explain: Words ending in x add -es: box – boxes.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to a word ending in x

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'baby'?
quiz.explain: Change y to ies: baby – babies.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change y to ies

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'leaf'?
quiz.explain: 'leaf' changes to 'leaves'.
quiz.mistake: Just adds -s to a word that changes

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'child'?
quiz.explain: 'child' becomes 'children'. It does not take -s.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to a special word

quiz.q: Which word is plural?
quiz.explain: 'puddles' means more than one puddle.
steps: 'puddles' ends in -s and means many puddles.
quiz.mistake: Does not look for the -s ending that shows more than one

quiz.q: Fill in: 'Two paper ___ are floating in the puddle.'
quiz.explain: 'Two' means more than one, so we use the plural 'boats'.
quiz.mistake: Uses the singular after a number bigger than one

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'foot'?
quiz.explain: 'foot' becomes 'feet'. It is a special plural.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to a word that changes its vowels

teach.ask: Gappu has one nest. His friend has three. He asks: 'Is it nests or nestes? How do plurals work?'
teach.praise: Nests! One nest, three nests! Yay!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what plural means and when we add -s or -es?

revise.summary: Singular means one and plural means more than one. Most words add -s, words ending in s, sh, ch or x add -es, some y words change to ies, and some words change in a special way.
focus: Choosing singular or plural to fit a sentence
remember: boat – boats; box – boxes; dish – dishes
child – children; leaf – leaves; foot – feet
